definitions.explanation: A square pit cut into the floor of a traditional Japanese house, used for heating and cooking. Charcoal or wood is burned in it, and a pot can be hung above it.

examples.japanese: {囲炉裏|いろり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{囲|かこ}む→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧。
{囲炉裏|いろり}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}いた→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
examples.english: I grilled fish over the hearth.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{民家|みんか}→民家：13217_minka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{囲炉裏|いろり}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦そこ→そこ：00991_soko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{集|あつ}まって→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Old farmhouses had a sunken hearth where the family would gather to eat.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The {囲炉裏|いろり} was the center of daily life in traditional Japanese homes, serving as a source of warmth, a place to cook, and a gathering spot for the family. Today they are rarely found in modern homes but can be seen in traditional inns (⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧), folk museums, and rural restaurants. Some modern restaurants feature {囲炉裏|いろり}-style seating as an atmosphere element.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {囲炉裏|いろり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{囲|かこ}む→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧: to gather around the hearth
- {囲炉裏|いろり}{端|ばた}: by the hearth
- {囲炉裏|いろり}⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧: hearth-cooked cuisine
